content:
maya: quick FYI — a new user hit a blocker on the ruby quickstart. README step about `bundle exec` points at the old auth helper and fails with `undefined method 'refresh!'`

olivia: oh no. do you have the exact diff they followed? link?

maya: pasted from their repro: `gem 'redwood', '~> 0.3'` then README says to run `bundle exec ruby quickstart.rb` and the quickstart references `Auth::RefreshableToken.new` which we removed in 0.4.0. they were on macOS + rbenv.

sam: thanks for catching. this is a doc/compat mismatch — we updated SDK surface but forgot to update minimal sampleapp. quick repro on my laptop takes 30s. can we patch README + add a smoke CI?

olivia: +1 to CI smoke. Maya, can you open a tiny PR that updates the quickstart snippet to use the new `Redwood::Auth::Client.new(token_refresh: ...)` pattern? Should be 3-line change.

maya: will do. adding a note to mention `gem 'redwood', '>= 0.4.0'` instead of `~> 0.3`.

kevin: also flagging for the release notes — this is a breaking devex change that will hit newbies. maybe add a migration note under "Upgrading the Ruby SDK".

maya: yup I'll add migration note in the README and create a small test in .github/workflows/quickstart-smoke.yml that runs `bundle install && bundle exec ruby quickstart.rb` on linux matrix.

sam: if you want a quick patch snippet, use:```diff
- gem 'redwood', '~> 0.3'
+ gem 'redwood', '>= 0.4.0'
```
and replace `Auth::RefreshableToken.new` with `Redwood::Auth::Client.new` in quickstart.rb (and show example `client.refresh_credentials` call).

olivia: can you also throw a note in the PR description: "reasons: auth surface changed in 0.4.0; adds smoke workflow". i'll review asap.

maya: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ruby-quickstart/pull/72 — patch + smoke workflow. tagged @olivia for review. :tada:

ci-bot: Build queued for PR #72 — ruby-matrix (2 jobs)

ci-bot: Job ruby-2.7 on ubuntu-latest: PASSED :white_check_mark:

ci-bot: Job ruby-3.1 on ubuntu-latest: FAILED — bundler conflict on platform-specific gem (nokogiri). output: `nokogiri requires ffi (~> 1.15)`

sam: ok the smoke test caught a separate nokogiri platform issue. maya — can you change workflow to use ruby/setup-ruby with bundler cache disabled or pin nokogiri platform? alternatively switch quickstart to use pure stdlib for the tiny example to avoid native gems.

maya: for speed I'll switch the quickstart to a minimal net/http call + json parse to avoid extra deps. will update PR.

olivia: perfect. after tweak i'll merge. also adding a short note in the onboarding docs so support doesn't get the same ticket again.

kevin: thanks all. small threads like this really cut down first-run churn. :clap:
